📖 0% read

arXiv:2611.23495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Call option prices, viewed as functions of strike and time-to-expiration, are totally positive of order 2 (TP2) if the ratio of the price of a higher-strike call to a lower-strike call increases with time-to-expiration. A corresponding property applies to put option prices. Prior work has developed conditions for these properties to hold for European options; here we establish these properties for American options. The key condition we require is that log returns on the underlying asset have a log-concave density. Gaussian densities provide an notable special case. Within our framework, we show that total positivity properties hold more broadly for American than European options. Empirically, we find that violations of TP2 properties are infrequent, typically small, and reverse quickly. Trades that bet against violations achieve high hit rates. Violations are more frequent among European than American options, a pattern that is qualitatively consistent with our theoretical results.

AI, Specialization, and the Organization of Knowledge Work: Evidence from Legal Services

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (236 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

According to recent reports, arXiv:2611.23354v1 Announce Type: newly introduced Abstract: Artificial intelligence makes specialized knowledge cheaper to use, but its effects on professional-service firms depend on how clients reallocate work and how suppliers respond. We develop a framework linking individual self-provision, enterprise make-or-buy decisions, and pricing by specialist firms. As AI improves lower-priced alternatives, clients may reallocate work across outside providers without bringing it in-house. If the departing work is more price-sensitive than the work that remains, premium firms may raise their optimal markups even as their share of work declines. We examine these margins in U.S. legal services. Across 89 federal districts, a difference-in-differences analysis finds a 6.6-percentage-point increase in non-prisoner self-representation relative to prisoner petitions by fiscal 2025, remaining substantial after adjusting for pre-existing trends. In contrast, lawyer employment shows no clear post-2022 shift toward client firms. Legal-AI benchmarks reveal continuing limitations in reliably completing complex, multi-step work, offering one possible explanation. Meanwhile, the largest law firms reported 13% revenue growth in 2025 despite nearly flat billable hours, while lower-priced firms experienced stronger demand growth. Reported AI integration is also stronger among firms with lower revenue per lawyer. These patterns highlight the importance of changes in work allocation and supplier competition, even as much of the underlying reallocation predates generative AI. The findings illustrate why cheaper expertise need not produce either widespread internalization or declining prices for premium professional services.

Industry News: Amazon RDS now supports fast storage volume initialization

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that amazon RDS now initializes storage volumes faster when you perform a point-in-time restore (PITR), create a read replica, or convert a Single-AZ instance to Multi-AZ.
  • Previously, the initialization rate varied with your workload and with which blocks were accessed.
  • In a recent development, fast storage volume initialization is enabled by default and no action is required.

Sources indicate that amazon RDS now initializes storage volumes faster when you perform a point-in-time restore (PITR), create a read replica, or convert a Single-AZ instance to Multi-AZ. Each of these operations creates storage volumes from a snapshot, and the data blocks are downloaded from Amazon S3 before you can access them. With fast storage volume initialization, you get a fully performant DB instance in a predictable amount of time.

Previously, the initialization rate varied with your workload and with which blocks were accessed. As there was no dedicated bandwidth, so you could see increased I/O latency and had no way to tell when an instance would reach full performance. Now, each database instance is initialized at up to 4 TiB per hour, across every gp3 and io2 storage volume attached to the instance. If concurrent initialization across your account exceeds the available bandwidth, the remaining blocks initialize on a best-effort basis, so initialization is never slower than today. Your DB instance stays available and usable while initialization runs.

In a recent development, fast storage volume initialization is enabled by default and no action is required. To follow progress, use the StorageOperationStatus and StorageOperationPercentProgress fields in the Amazon RDS console, the DescribeDBInstances API, the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS SDKs.

This capability is available at no additional cost for RDS for MariaDB, RDS for MySQL, RDS for PostgreSQL, RDS for Db2, RDS for Microsoft SQL Server, and RDS for Oracle, in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see Amazon RDS storage in the Amazon RDS User Guide.

Amazon CloudFront Functions can now make network calls and act on the response during a request. CloudFront Functions runs lightweight JavaScript at CloudFront edge locations to customize requests and responses. Previously, if your logic depended on data from another service, you had to use Lambda@Edge or move that logic to your origin. Now your functions can use real-time data to personalize, authenticate, or route requests at the edge, close to your viewers.

Recent findings suggest that with the latest cf.fetch() method, your functions can call your API endpoints and use the response to decide how to handle each request. For example, you can check an AI agent's permissions and usage budget so that only authorized requests reach your API or MCP server, or send request signals to a security or fraud detection service to block or challenge bad traffic. With cf.beacon(), you can send analytics events in the background without slowing down viewers, even for content served from cache. Both methods take advantage of the origin settings already on your distribution, including origin access control (OAC), VPC origins, and connection reuse.

It has been revealed that network calls are available at all CloudFront edge locations. They cost $0.10 per million calls, on top of CloudFront Functions invocation charges, and are included at no additional cost in the Pro plan and above in CloudFront flat-rate prepares. Amazon RDS for MySQL 9.7 launches with community MySQL 9.7.4. This launch introduces support for the Replication Applier Metrics component, JSON Duality Views, and Hypergraph Optimizer.

The Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction. JSON Duality Views let applications read and write the same relational tables as JSON documents. The Hypergraph Optimizer is an opt-in query optimizer that can improve execution plans for complex, multi-join queries. For more details, refer to the MySQL 9.7.4 release notes and the Amazon RDS for MySQL release notes.

You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon RDS User Guide. Amazon RDS for MySQL makes it simple to set up, operate, and scale MySQL deployments in the cloud. Create or patch a fully managed Amazon RDS database in the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

Previously, you had to build and maintain your own export and restore process, and restored users received new identifiers and had to reset their passwords.

With PITR, you choose a recovery point, preview how many customers, groups, multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings, and passkeys the recovery will create, upgrade, or delete, and then start or cancel the recovery. Recovered users keep their identifiers, passwords, MFA settings, and passkeys, so they can sign in without resetting their credentials. For example, if a script deletes or modifies users by mistake, you can restore the user data to the moment before it ran.

Today, Amazon SageMaker AI reveals cross-Region inference routing, which helps keep inference applications available when a region runs short of capacity by sending requests to endpoints deployed in other AWS Regions and AWS accounts. Models served on accelerated instances can reach capacity limits in a single Region, and an unhealthy endpoint can lead to throttling and errors for end customers. Previously, teams had to build and maintain their own routing, health checks, and retry logic across Regions. With cross-Region inference routing in SageMaker AI, developers create an inference router, register the real-time endpoints, asynchronous endpoints, and inference components they already run, and point their applications at the router. The router prefers endpoints in its own Region, shifts latest requests to healthy destinations in other Regions as errors rise, and returns traffic gradually after the local endpoint recovers. Existing endpoints, models, and containers do not change. Endpoint owners stay in control: an endpoint policy determines which routers in other accounts can use an endpoint, and an optional cross-Region traffic cap reserves capacity for the endpoint’s local callers. Each real-time response identifies the endpoint that served the request and the reason, and router metrics in Amazon CloudWatch show where traffic went. Cross-Region inference routing is available for real-time inference in 32 commercial AWS Regions, and for asynchronous inference in 25 Regions. There is no additional charge for cross-Region inference routing. Customers pay standard SageMaker AI pricing for the endpoints that serve requests and standard Amazon CloudWatch rates for router metrics. To learn more, see the Amazon SageMaker AI Developer Guide and SageMaker AI Deployment page.

In a recent development, the agent takes the job's configuration, logs, and Spark telemetry together with your chosen goal and returns recommendations computed by a deterministic recommendation engine. The engine reads all job artifacts together to identify what is driving runtime and cost: too little parallelism, a skewed join key, memory pressure forcing spill, idle executors, or capacity provisioned beyond what the job uses. When cost and performance trade off, the agent improves the metric you chose while keeping any regression of the other within defined limits. The engine also checks best practices such as platform-level improvements like upgrading to a newer AWS Glue version or using AWS Graviton processors. Each recommendation is labeled by the area it modifies: infrastructure, Spark configuration, code, or data layout. All access is authenticated with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and logged in AWS CloudTrail.

Recent findings suggest that the Apache Spark Optimization Agent is available at no additional charge for AWS Glue versions 4.0 and later in all Regions where AWS Glue is available, except the AWS GovCloud (US) and China Regions. Sources indicate that today, AWS AppConfig introduces two new configuration profile types to help you manage the settings for your generative AI applications: AI model invocation configurations, and AI prompt configurations. You can now change model settings and prompts while your application is running, without redeploying code. These updates use AWS AppConfig's safe deployment practices, including gradual rollouts and automatic rollback. This can allow you to move faster and safer, and avoid unexpected behaviors and tokenomics results with rapidly evolving AI solutions.

AI model invocation configurations store the settings your application uses to call an AI model. These include the model identifier, inference parameters such as temperature and maximum tokens, and messages such as system prompts and example conversation turns. Provider-specific options are managed in custom parameters, so the same schema works across AI providers. Similarly, AI prompt configurations store prompts as separately versioned artifacts. You can update  and optimize a prompt on its own,without changing the model configuration, and reuse it across multiple applications. This allows for powerful prompt engineering.

You can roll out a change to these gradually, for example to 10%, then 20%, then 30% of your traffic. Along the way, you can measure the change's effect on operational metrics, customer experience, and token usage. If an alarm in Amazon CloudWatch, Datadog, New Relic, or another observability solution goes off during the rollout, AWS AppConfig can automatically roll the change back to the previous state.

AI model invocation and AI prompt configurations are available today in all AWS Regions where AWS AppConfig is available, at no additional cost. To get started, see Creating an AI model invocation configuration profile and Creating an AI prompt configuration profile in the AWS AppConfig User Guide.

Industry News: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that waymo is at the moment restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars’ driving behavior on highways.
  • This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem.
  • In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that waymo is at the moment restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars’ driving behavior on highways. Specifically, the software tends to drive into construction zones at speed. As first reported by the San Francisco Business Times, this behavior actually drew the ire of California’s DMV earlier this month, which ordered Waymo to stop driving on Californian highways immediately and until it can convince the DMV that its cars no longer “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.”.

This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem. In Arizona, Waymo robotaxis did not recognize ramp closure signs on six occasions in Phoenix in April and entered construction zones. A month later in California, seven Waymo robotaxis entered lanes with active construction. In June, Waymo recalled the almost 3,800 robotaxis capable of highway driving. That problem led Waymo to stick to surface streets only in California after the May incidents until late July, when the robotaxis resumed highway operations.

In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.”.

Waymo also told the government that the updated software is better able to respond to emergency vehicles when in a construction zone and that the tech giant has made “operational changes that better identify and mitigate potential entry into pre-planned construction zones and enable more Remote Assistance capability” if it happens again.

Which it has. Despite the update to improve behavior around emergency vehicles, a video went viral in early November showing a Waymo robotaxi on I-280 driving past a pair of California Highway Patrol cars conducting a rolling roadblock as they held traffic behind a slow-moving construction vehicle. California also says there was an incident in which a Waymo robotaxi entered a construction zone on US 101 near Burlingame.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Waymo told Ars. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

Waymo also told Ars it was continuing to work with the various California agencies that regulate transport.

Until the suspension, Waymo was only conducting highway operations in Los Angeles and the Bay Area in California, as well as in Arizona.

  • Lambda durable functions extend Lambda's event-driven programming model with operations that checkpoint progress automatically and pause execution for up to one year when waiting on external events.
  • Industry observers note that the SDK works with the Rust tools developers already use.

Industry observers note that today, AWS introduces the general availability of the open source AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust. Rust developers can use the SDK to build resilient, long-running workflows using Lambda durable functions, to create multi-step applications like infrastructure automation, deployment rollouts with approval gates, and pipelines that call AI models and pause for human review directly in their Rust code without implementing custom progress tracking.

Lambda durable functions extend Lambda's event-driven programming model with operations that checkpoint progress automatically and pause execution for up to one year when waiting on external events. With the SDK, developers write a durable function as an ordinary async Rust function that awaits each durable operation like any other future and can run independent operations concurrently. The SDK includes steps that save their results, callbacks for human-in-the-loop and agent-in-the-loop workflows, invocations of other durable functions, and timed waits.

Industry observers note that the SDK works with the Rust tools developers already use. Developers add the aws-durable-execution-sdk crate with cargo add, build with Cargo Lambda, and deploy a single binary on the provided.al2023 runtime. Before deploying, they can test complete workflows with cargo test and the SDK's LocalRunner without requiring network access or AWS credentials.

To get started, see the Lambda durable functions developer guide, the Rust SDK guide, and the AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust on GitHub. For Regional availability and pricing details for Lambda durable functions, see the AWS Capabilities by Region page and AWS Lambda Pricing.

  • The new information released by ULA confirms reporting from Ars Technica on Tuesday that the rocket’s failure was not due to the performance of the vehicle’s main engines, which are provided by Blue Origin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Launch Alliance stated Wednesday that the failure of its Vulcan rocket during a launch on Sunday was caused by inadequate fuel supply.

Industry observers note that “ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday,” the company said in a statement. “While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines.”.

The new information released by ULA confirms reporting from Ars Technica on Tuesday that the rocket’s failure was not due to the performance of the vehicle’s main engines, which are provided by Blue Origin.

This represents an vital revelation from ULA and will provide some major relief to different parts of the US aerospace community, particularly Blue Origin and NASA.

That’s because the BE-4 engine is also the bedrock of Blue Origin’s Upcoming Glenn rocket. This powerful rocket uses a similar but slightly more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. New Glenn experienced its own catastrophic failure in May during a ground test, a failure that was later attributed to a main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines.

After this anomaly, Blue Origin retrofitted the main oxygen valve, including for Vulcan missions. Now it’s clear that this retrofit was not implicated in the Vulcan accident. With the preliminary Vulcan investigation having largely exonerated the BE-4 engine, Blue Origin can press ahead with its return-to-flight mission with Newly introduced Glenn, which could occur as soon as January.

“Following the Vulcan anomaly, Blue Origin immediately worked alongside ULA to review flight data and support the investigation,” Blue Origin said in a statement Wednesday. “Together, we identified that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines. ULA is a valued partner, and we look forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.”.

Amid a worsening US launch crunch, Latest Glenn offers the most tangible option for near-term relief for satellite operators, including Amazon Leo, which lost dozens of satellites on Sunday. The heavy-lift rocket has many commercial and government customers lined up for launch. NASA in particular is counting on the rocket to launch a number of lunar missions in the next two years, as well as play a significant role in landing humans on the Moon later this decade.

Sources indicate that also a relief to NASA will be confirmation that Vulcan’s upper stage, the Centaur V, did not contribute to the failure. NASA recently contracted with ULA to use the Centaur V as its fresh upper stage for the Space Launch System rocket, enabling future missions to the Moon.

For ULA, however, the latest revision only brings more challenges.

It has been revealed that vulcan represents the firm’s great hope to remain relevant in a US launch industry increasingly dominated by SpaceX and newer entrants such as Blue Origin. With Vulcan on the sidelines, other companies, such as Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and Stoke Space, could also elbow out the once all-powerful launch firm.

Sources indicate that although Sunday’s Vulcan flight, its fifth overall, was the first outright mission failure for the rocket, two previous rolls out also experienced problems. Those concerns involved the nozzle of the solid rocket boosters. ULA has now spent three years trying to move the rocket out of its teething phase and into regular operations. A successful launch on Sunday could have set up at least a monthly launch cadence next year.

In a recent development, now, the cash-strapped tech giant must also contend with a fresh concern involving propellant management and complicated plumbing that feeds liquid oxygen and methane to the BE-4 engines. It will certainly be offline for several months.

  • Account Tagging for SaaS Products is available for products with a SaaS listing on AWS Marketplace.

Recent findings suggest that AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS introduces Account Tagging for SaaS Products for AWS Revenue Measurement. Partners can now measure the AWS revenue impact of their SaaS solutions by tagging the AWS accounts that host them, instead of tagging individual resources.

It has been revealed that until now, Partners with SaaS listings measured that impact through Resource Tagging, User Agent strings, or AWS Marketplace Metering. With Account Tagging for SaaS products, a Partner uses AWS Organizations to tag partner-owned member accounts dedicated to a single SaaS product. The tag key is aws-apn-id- and the tag value is pc:. AWS Revenue Measurement then attributes all eligible AWS consumption in each tagged account to that product.

Account Tagging for SaaS Products is available for products with a SaaS listing on AWS Marketplace. Each tagged account must be dedicated to one product. Partners whose products share an account can continue to use Resource Tagging, User Agent string, or Identity Tagging. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more about implementing AWS Revenue Measurement, review the onboarding guide for more information.

It shouldn’t be this easy to pedal 25 mph: Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I’ve had only one experience of pedaling an e-bike after it ran out of juice, but it was enough to make checking the battery display an anxiety-driven habit: “Can I afford to use the highest assist level up this hill?
  • These aren’t fun questions to have rattling around in your head while riding home in the dark.
  • But those intrusive thoughts never crossed my mind while I was testing Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I’ve had only one experience of pedaling an e-bike after it ran out of juice, but it was enough to make checking the battery display an anxiety-driven habit: “Can I afford to use the highest assist level up this hill? Should I switch to eco mode to preserve power and make sure I have enough to get home with the bike lights on?”.

These aren’t fun questions to have rattling around in your head while riding home in the dark.

But those intrusive thoughts never crossed my mind while I was testing Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo. I didn’t experience range anxiety, even while blowing through city streets at 25-plus mph (40.2 kph). The bike has so much juice (840 watt-hours) and power (810 watts of peak power and 105 newton-meters of torque) from Specialized’s 3.1 motor system that I could ride as far and as fast as I wanted without worrying about having enough battery to get back home.

Given my preference for biking over driving, I need a bike that can get me across town at a decent clip without draining an entire charge. That’s exactly what the Evo delivered on my longest rides.

What sold me on the bike was a 24-mile round trip that took 83 minutes and used just 56 percent of the battery. According to Specialized’s app, which connects to the bike over Bluetooth, I averaged 235 W of assist power while moving an average of 17 mph, though I was generally closer to 20 mph on stretches where I didn’t have to slow down. I also hit a max speed of 27.3 mph with little effort.

The bike is a beast, weighing around 70 pounds for the large-size frame I tested. Despite being the heaviest e-bike I’ve ridden, the Evo makes pedaling easier than ever. The bike lacks a throttle, so it takes a few rotations to get moving, but once the assist kicks in, it’s remarkable how easily you can reach the 18–20 mph range.

In a recent development, that higher speed comes from the bike’s Sport mode, which became my default setting. It requires a bit more pedaling to reach full assist, which explains why my smartwatch recorded my heart rate in the moderate-to-vigorous zone if I was riding above 20 mph. The other modes are Eco (minimal assist, with you supplying most of the power), Turbo (max power with little effort, making uphill climbs trivial), and Auto (which adjusts assist level to your pedaling). You can also tune each setting to your liking.

Recent findings suggest that the added bulk is also meant to handle rougher terrain. I’ve had the occasional flat tire from road debris on slimmer bikes, so I appreciate the sturdier, all-terrain, flat-resistant tires. Still, the 70-pound frame makes me hesitant to venture too far from pavement. I won’t be bombing down any mountain bike trails, but it’s helpful to have the option to jump off a curb or ride on dirt or gravel roads.

Industry observers note that the weight makes the bike markedly different from the previous Turbo Vado we reviewed; this isn’t a bike I’d want to ride without assistance. Even the Eco mode, which you’d have to use exclusively to get the bike’s purported 150-km (93-mile), five-hour range, felt a bit sluggish compared to the more powerful modes I preferred. Specialized also sells a 280-Whr range extender, but at $700, it feels like overkill.

In a recent development, the RockShox Psylo suspension fork, with 120 mm of travel, also made this the smoothest-riding e-bike I’ve tested. Other e-bikes I’ve ridden have felt stiff over even small bumps in the road, but the Evo’s bounciness made hitting bumps feel like a nice change of pace. I used to be scared of going over a curb, and that’s no longer the case. The 40 mm dropper seatpost is another nice feature, giving riders a bit of travel and letting them lower the seat to make it easier to touch the ground when stopped or dismounting.

Credit: Specialized Credit: Specialized.

While other e-bikes I’ve owned initially offered good range, storing them in colder weather has been an matter for their longevity.

So I’m grateful that Specialized made the downtube battery removable. Being able to store the battery in my house helps since I keep my bikes in an outdoor shed—I no longer have to worry about it sitting in freezing temperatures. A full charge takes four hours, though you can tweak the battery to cap charging at 80 percent to further extend its life.

Sources indicate that the other electric components are nice, too. On the Evo 5.0 I rode, a touchscreen lets you cycle through ride data, including your speed, estimated range remaining, and power assistance level. The front light even comes with low-beam (450 lumens) and high-beam (805 lumens) settings, making my night rides more visible.

If I have any complaints about my time with this bike, they boil down to two things. First, it’s incredibly heavy, making it difficult for many people to take up stairs. Second, the convenience of riding at high speed and making quick journeys has left my road bike gathering dust unless I’m specifically going out for a workout (and those are harder now that I’m so accustomed to riding the Evo). That’s more of a personal glitch than a mark against the bike, though. It’s fun to ride, but maybe at the cost of consistent manual pedaling.

And then there’s the cost. I tested the Evo 5.0 ($5,200), which sits between the 4.0 ($4,500) and 6.0 ($7,000) in terms of cost, performance, and features. At $5,200, though, I would’ve liked to see a phone mount on the 5.0, which is a common enough feature on less-expensive bikes.

Those prices make securing the bike even more notable, and Specialized offers a few safety features to thwart theft. As mentioned, you can remove the battery, lock the back wheel, and disable the power system; there’s also Apple Find My integration if the bike ever escapes your purview (a bummer if you use Android, though).

In all, Specialized has upgraded the e-bike experience enough for me to want to upgrade, though the price makes me blanch a bit. Maybe I can subsidize a purchase by selling an older e-bike.

#9774. The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1689 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1689 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts.
  • After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991.
  • In a recent development, but the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.

After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.

In a recent development, but the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.

The US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.).

Recent findings suggest that for their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.).

According to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data shows that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.

It has been revealed that the full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.

The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.

But Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer said the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.

Sources indicate that in a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.

Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.

It has been revealed that brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas—that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.

In a recent development, “Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer noted, and the national data highlights multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.

Sources indicate that for people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the big outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.

Recent findings suggest that data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in big outbreaks in Arizona and Utah. But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”.

Sources indicate that to date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.

For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.

In a recent development, but in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he said.

In a recent development, with the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action strategy” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.

While the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.

Recent findings suggest that A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. Meanwhile, non-medical exemptions from school vaccination requirements have never been higher, at 4 percent. Currently, 24 states have exemption rates at or above 5 percent, meaning that even if they are able to vaccinate every single non-exempt child, they would still not meet the 95 percent target. And this is just the data for young children. The vaccination coverage for adults is another concern, and the data there is scarce. In Pennsylvania’s massive outbreak, 1,055 of the 1,561 cases this year have been in adults ages 18 and older (less than 1 percent of the cases were fully vaccinated).

While some health officials have noted optimistically that 92.4 percent in children is just a few percentage points from the target, the reality of bringing up vaccination rates is more onerous.

PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa stressed the point in the press briefing Tuesday: It’s “not the national average or the average in the state or even the average in a major city, you need to guarantee that in every community, village, you have this vaccination coverage up to 95 percent. This is very crucial,” Barbosa remarked.

It has been revealed that the point has been demonstrated in the US. In 2019, the US came very close to losing its measles elimination status. Unlike now—when the virus is on a nationwide rampage, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases—in 2019, the US nearly lost its status from a single, large outbreak that spread in New York. Though it didn’t explode on a national level, it took 11 months to stamp out in those undervaccinated communities. In that year, the US reported 1,274 measles cases total.

Industry observers note that the situation in the US has only gotten worse, and the outlook is bleak, Brewer warns. “The measles outbreaks in Canada and Mexico are winding down,” he noted. “However, in the US, our measles problem continues to accelerate. There is no end in sight.”.

  • With source actions in AWS Transform, you define each action once, run it in bulk on the servers and waves you choose, and reuse it across accounts and migrations.
  • This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform for migrations is available.

AWS Transform now automates the tasks that prepare and validate your servers during a migration, before they move and after they launch on AWS. AWS Transform is the agentic AI service that speeds up cloud migration, application modernization, and continuous tech debt reduction. With the newly introduced source actions capability, you can create actions and run them securely on your source servers at the right point in the migration, from the early stages through cutover. Post-launch actions complement this by automatically configuring and validating each workload as soon as it rolls out on AWS.

With source actions in AWS Transform, you define each action once, run it in bulk on the servers and waves you choose, and reuse it across accounts and migrations. AWS Transform manages these actions centrally, so you can reuse them across accounts and migrations instead of rebuilding them each time. You can monitor the status of each action and confirm your go/no-go decision before moving to the next step. Source preparation and post-launch actions are now part of the migration plan itself, so you no longer have to coordinate and run these activities by hand.

This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform for migrations is available. To get started, see the AWS Transform documentation or visit the AWS Transform product page.

Industry News: Trump admin orders Kalshi to halt wagers on what words Trump will say

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (958 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date.
  • CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.
  • In a recent development, the markets taken down by Kalshi allowed customers to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date. Kalshi halted trading in the contracts while the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) conducts a review into whether the Trump mention contracts violate federal law.

CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.

In a recent development, the markets taken down by Kalshi allowed customers to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies. A similar expired event contract that can still be viewed on Kalshi’s website asked whether Trump would use the nicknames “Marjorie Traitor Greene,” “Sleepy Joe,” and “Whack Job” or “Wack Job” before April 2026.

The CFTC order issued to Kalshi last week applies broadly to “the TRUMPSAY contract series.” The event contracts in this series include trades in the format, “Will [word] be said by Donald Trump after Issuance and before [date]?” The CFTC order also applied to a specific event contract that asks, “What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?”.

Sources indicate that the CFTC order came several months after the federal agency settled charges against a Trump teleprompter aide who made over $100,000 in Kalshi wagers on what Trump would say in prepared remarks. On August 28, the CFTC required the man, Gabriel Perez, to disgorge profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil penalty of $65,000.

“In his position, Perez had access to presidential speeches prior to those speeches being delivered and Perez misappropriated that information—in breach of his duty of trust and confidence—to trade presidential mention market contracts, generating over $107,500 in profits,” the CFTC said at the time.

Senate Democrats recently said the White House hasn’t taken meaningful action against insider trading, “all while the president and his family stand to personally profit from their participation in prediction markets.” Prediction markets have flourished under the Trump administration’s permissive regulatory approach. The CFTC has allowed prediction markets to offer sports gambling nationwide and filed lawsuits against states that attempt to regulate Kalshi under their gambling laws.

Kalshi recently dropped Donald Trump Jr. as an advisor, saying it made the decision because Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm increased its investment in its competitor, Polymarket. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour also acknowledged that the “optics” of Trump Jr.’s advisory role weren’t good for Kalshi. Trump Jr. still stands to benefit from Kalshi’s success, because he was given equity shares in the company.

The CFTC has noted that mention markets are easily manipulated but reviews them on a case-by-case basis instead of prohibiting them. Prediction markets can “self-certify” that any upcoming event contract complies with US law and start offering it without waiting for the CFTC’s permission, but the CFTC can halt trading afterward based on reviews of specific contracts.

Sources indicate that the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) prohibits the listing of contracts that are readily susceptible to manipulation. CFTC staff issued a September advisory about the legality of markets on what people will say, and whether they will attend an event or interact with another person. The advisory said these contracts may be viewed as “presumptively readily susceptible to manipulation,” because they “may be controlled by a single individual, a small group of individuals, or persons with access to or influence over the individual whose words, attendance, or interaction determines settlement.”.

Sources indicate that the CFTC stated this type of contract requires measures “to prevent manipulation and misappropriation of material non-public information,” and that Kalshi failed to comply with the CFTC staff advisory. About “a week after the Staff Advisory was released, Kalshi listed the Contract [on nicknames] for trading without amending the [TRUMPSAY] Contract Series’ self-certification (or submitting a fresh self-certification) to make the ‘heightened showing’ of non-manipulability required by the Staff Advisory,” the order said.

The CFTC stated it will conduct “a proceeding to determine whether the certification of the Contracts was false—that is, whether the Contracts comply with the Act, including the Core Principles, and Commission regulations thereunder as Kalshi has certified.” So far, “Kalshi has not adequately demonstrated that the Contracts are not readily susceptible to manipulation” as required by law, the order said.

“Given the available supporting evidence, including that Kalshi has not attempted to establish that the Contracts are non-manipulable with respect to the Staff Advisory’s guidance, the Commission presumptively believes the certification is false,” the order noted.

It has been revealed that the CFTC order is not a determination on whether the Trump mention markets can meet the standard of not being readily susceptible to manipulation. Rather, it is a determination that Kalshi has so far failed to show that the contracts are not easily manipulated.

The order “resolves only that, based on the current record, Kalshi has not demonstrated that the Contracts as certified comply with the Act and that the Contracts should not trade while the Commission completes its review,” the CFTC mentioned.

We contacted Kalshi and will upgrade this article if it provides a response.

Sources indicate that mansour defended the Trump mention contracts at an Axios event on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg. “What the president does say moves markets,” Mansour mentioned. “So predicting what he’s about to say is actually pretty meaningful.”.

The Bloomberg article noted that “Kalshi’s main rival Polymarket still has live mention markets tied to Trump’s speeches on its international website, which is not regulated by the CFTC.” Polymarket offers a separate US-regulated version of its prediction market.

According to recent reports, customers can now use Amazon EC2 performance status checks and latest utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring to observe and act on the performance of their EC2 workloads without setup within the instance, complementing their in-guest tooling. Customers running performance-sensitive EC2 workloads can use these signals to monitor their CPU and GPU resources, tune capacity needs, and troubleshoot application issues.

According to recent reports, EC2 performance status checks identify nonterminal hardware conditions that impact performance on accelerated computing instances. These checks also recommend an action, such as rebooting to complete GPU memory row remapping without replacing the instance. The additions to Detailed Monitoring include support for OpenTelemetry metrics, one-minute GPU metrics that help teams tune accelerated workloads, and a new, higher resolution 10-second CPU utilization metric that helps customers size and scale compute capacity using EC2 Application Auto Scaling. Customers can selectively opt into these new metrics using categories that they can easily apply to their instances across their fleet. Together, these new capabilities make it easier for customers to manage their compute resources.

Sources indicate that EC2 performance status checks are available at no additional charge. EC2 Detailed Monitoring metrics are opt-in and incur standard CloudWatch charges for EC2 Detailed Monitoring. These capabilities are available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions.

To learn more, see EC2 Detailed Monitoring documentation and EC2 performance status checks documentation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Best Buy website’s movie section currently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” New titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025).
  • Most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Best Buy is selling Blu-rays directly through its website and in physical stores again after exiting Blu-ray and DVD sales in 2023.

The Best Buy website’s movie section currently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” New titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025). Best Buy is also selling some older titles on Blu-ray, including It’s a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972).

Most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days. As of this writing, The Odyssey appears to be in stock at Best Buy stores, as it’s presently listed as available for pickup within as little as an hour.

Ars Technica reached out to Best Buy to ask whether customers can expect the store to continue selling Blu-rays moving forward.

In October 2023, Best Buy confirmed that it would stop selling Blu-rays and DVDs online and in stores starting in 2024.

In a recent development, “To state the obvious, the way we watch movies and TV reveals is much different today than it was decades ago. Making this change gives us more space and opportunity to bring customers upcoming and innovative tech for them to explore, discover and enjoy,” a Best Buy spokesperson mentioned in a statement issued at the time.

Last year, the Best Buy website started selling Blu-rays and DVDs from third parties via its online marketplace.

Numerous other companies have reduced or ended their Blu-ray and/or DVD businesses in recent years. Target, for instance, only sells the discs in stores during special occasions (like holidays or for significant releases) now. Disney outsourced its DVD and Blu-ray business to Sony, which subsequently stopped selling recordable Blu-rays to people, and DVD rental tech giant Redbox went out of business.

It has been revealed that that noted, physical media, including Blu-rays and DVDs, still have a place in many people’s homes. Because digital copies of movies and shows can be plucked from online platforms and people’s libraries that were previously “purchased” (but truly only rented) without warning, enthusiasts continue relying on physical media. Enthusiasts also opt for physical copies of movies and shows for better picture and/or sound quality than what’s available digitally, as well as for bragging rights.

Overall, the sales of Blu-rays and DVDs in the US have been steadily declining, and annual consumer spending dropped 9.3 percent from 2024 to 2025, according to the Digital Entertainment Group (DEG). During this same time, however, consumer spending on 4K Blu-ray discs specifically increased 12 percent year over year, per DEG.

A resurgence in Blu-ray sales has been associated with the growth of collectible SteelBooks, which are Blu-rays sold in collectible steel boxes, and Gen Z, which, in some cases, are even turning to video rental stores for Blu-rays and DVDs.

“We’re seeing a lot of evidence, including at the Criterion Mobile Closet, that more young people are thinking about physical media in a different way,” Peter Becker, president of Criterion, which sells Blu-rays and DVDs online, told the Los Angeles Times in February. “In an age where so much is available to us on demand, it becomes increasingly key to us.”.

It has been revealed that today, AWS Marketplace confirms the general availability of buyer approvals. This lets you decide which AWS Marketplace purchases need sign-off, who approves them, and where approval happens. You can define buying policies for the conditions that matter to you, such as purchase amount, product type, pricing, and whether an offer is public or private. Additionally, you can choose to route each purchase request to the right place: the AWS Marketplace console, a chain of approvers by email, or your procurement system in Coupa or SAP Ariba.

When you route approvals by email, procurement, finance, legal, and cloud governance teams can approve requests without needing to sign into the AWS console. They see the product, price, terms, and can approve right from their email. For example, you can route large software commitments to Coupa or SAP Ariba for review, send mid-size purchases to multiple approvers by email, and let low-cost or pay-as-you-go purchases go through without approval. When a purchase is routed to your procurement system, it follows your existing approval flows and gets a dedicated purchase order for cleaner spend tracking and reconciliation.

With AWS Marketplace, customers can already choose which subset of available products their teams can buy, track each purchase with purchase orders, and require their employees to enter a purchase order when buying. Now, with buyer approvals, you can also control how each purchase is approved before making a financial commitment.

Customers can now create buying policies and approvals in all AWS Marketplace commercial Regions. To get started, see the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide.

Latest Update: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core.
  • It has been revealed that STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance.
  • Sources indicate that the new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core. Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft states is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG).

It has been revealed that STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: “The secure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened.”.

Sources indicate that the new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance.

This isn’t to say that system administrators won’t still have the final say on which security protocols are activated, just that the default package now ships in a pre-hardened state. Kerberos is now the default over NTLM, with protections added to LSASS; TLS is automatically restricted to modern cipher suites; key exchange uses “hybrid post-quantum key exchange” based on the quantum-safe ML-KEM; and remote desktop authentication and PowerShell script block logging get stricter as well.

Sources indicate that microsoft’s native NVMe storage stack was originally introduced via an update to Windows Server 2025, but it required administrators to enable it manually. The update eliminated NVMe translation through a SCSI stack while improving speeds and reducing overhead. The redesigned stack will now be default-on in Windows Server 2028.

Microsoft is upfront, noting that the newly introduced hardened security settings may break things due to software compatibility issues with older protocols, legacy authentication, or management tools and scripts. The company encourages users to try things and provide feedback about what goes wrong. “We want to hear where a hardened default gets in the way of a real workload: which setting, which application, and what you had to change to get it working,” the Windows Server Team noted in a blog post. “That is how the defaults get better before general availability.”.

It has been revealed that microsoft suggests that customers use the preview build as a test bed to determine where problems like compatibility still arise. This is not a release candidate build and shouldn’t be treated as such. Despite the new security stance that comes with the preview build, hardware-backed protections like Secure Boot and DMA requirements won’t be enforced until a later preview build. Kerberos is now the default preference over NTLM, but NTLM blocking itself will still have to wait for a later preview release.

Beyond those limitations, the current build has a known concern that cuts into its hardened goals. According to the release notes, “A race condition in the TLS hybrid key exchange implementation may cause the LSASS service to crash when hybrid groups are negotiated by a TLS server.” Microsoft recommends disabling hybrid-key exchange groups until the problem is addressed.

System administrators and curious homelabbers interested in testing the upcoming Windows Server 2028 can do so by registering with the Microsoft Windows Insider Program.

Industry observers note that AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS unveils Identity Tagging in AWS Revenue Measurement, a fresh way for Partners to get attributed revenue visibility for the AWS usage their solutions drive. Partners can now tag the IAM user or role their solution uses instead of tagging individual resources or decorating individual SDK/API calls. This makes attribution simpler and needs no code changes.

AWS Revenue Measurement then attributes usage from resources created by that identity to the Partner's product. Identity Tagging works alongside existing methods such as Resource Tagging, User Agent string, and SaaS Account Tagging, so Partners can pick the method that best fits their architecture.

AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more, review the AWS Revenue Measurement onboarding guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The streaming wars, or the battle to be the top streaming company, are ongoing, according to Ted Sarandos, a co-CEO of what many would consider today’s frontrunner.

But in an interview with Bloomberg published today, Sarandos noted that people are still spending significant time watching traditional broadcast TV.

“The streaming wars are continuing as we go. Half of television engagement in the United States is still linear, old television,” he mentioned, without specifying the source of the statistic. According to analysis from Nielsen, streaming represented 49.6 percent of TV viewing in August, with 36.4 percent coming from broadcast and cable. That still suggests a sizable amount of viewing time for streaming providers to target.

As Netflix seeks to strengthen its lead against rivals like YouTube and Skydance, there’s extra pressure for it to deliver hit reveals and movies.

Recent findings suggest that I think as Netflix has grown and matured and the business has grown and matured around us, that hit rate really matters. And you’ve got to get ahead of ‘are we on a path to continue [and] maintain that hit rate in the US particularly, but everywhere in the world?’ And I’d say the business is working everywhere in the world, including the US, but we should be doing better in the US than we were. And we’ve got to really focus on our ability to do that.

The CEO said that Netflix is focusing on “the ambition of storytelling” rather than “chasing everything that people just happen to spend five seconds on television on” or relying on AI-generated content.

“I think what’s going to happen is that people will desire more ambitious, more accomplished storytelling in a world that is flooded with slop,” Sarandos said.

Recent findings suggest that netflix has used generative AI-based workflows for various production tasks, like creating crowds or historical battle scenes, for hundreds of titles. This has helped Netflix save money while it increased the amount it spends on content this year by about 10 percent.

When it comes to streaming consumers struggling to find something to watch, Sarandos acknowledged that Netflix sometimes “make[s] mistakes about how we present new things” and can “bury things that you might be looking for under new things that you’re not coming for.” He pointed to AI as a tool for content discovery in addition to aiding in the pre-production and post-production of content.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump’s pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation.
  • Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA.
  • Recent findings suggest that in her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump’s pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation.

Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy’s decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats.

Recent findings suggest that in her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA’s current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn’t say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is “quite lethal” or that children are given vaccine doses the “size of a soda bottle.” Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong.

Axios quoted a senior Trump administration official as saying that Overton’s nomination was dropped because she “lacks the support on the Hill to move forward with her confirmation.”.

The Senate’s Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, chaired by Bill Cassidy (R-La.), was scheduled to vote on Overton’s nomination Wednesday. In a social media post Tuesday night, after her nomination was withdrawn, Cassidy noted he believed she had a “viable confirmation path.” But he said the nomination was “abandoned” after some anti-abortion senators sought commitments from her that they couldn’t get. “The Administration withdrew Dr. Overton rather than make such commitments,” Cassidy said.

“Unfortunately, with the limited time left, confirming a permanent FDA Commissioner will fall to Senate Democrats,” Cassidy noted.

After Overton’s last-minute withdrawal, the HELP committee’s agenda for Wednesday was updated again this morning to scrap a scheduled vote on Jim O’Neill, who was Trump’s nominee to run the NSF.

Recent findings suggest that O’Neill has been criticized for lacking the science experience needed to run the foundation. In the past, O’Neill worked as a Silicon Valley investor and entrepreneur and became a close ally of Peter Thiel. But under Trump, O’Neill has been the deputy secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services and served as acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. O’Neill took over the latter role after the former director, Susan Monarez, was ousted from it less than a month after her Senate confirmation. She later told Senators Kennedy fired her for refusing to blindly approve vaccine recommendations from his anti-vaccine advisors.

In a recent development, in remarks this morning, Cassidy said that O’Neill “did not do enough to stand up for science and against irresponsible decisions and statements from [Health] Secretary [Robert F.] Kennedy [Jr.].” As an example, Cassidy specifically referenced O’Neill’s role in the firing of Monarez. “Several members of the [HELP] committee had concerns regarding this,” Cassidy said.

“This time requires leadership and fortitude and standing up for what is right,” Cassidy added.

The NSF has been hard hit by the Trump administration and actions by Elon Musk’s DOGE. The NSF has been forced to cancel hundreds of research grants and taken brutal cuts to its budget and staff in the past two years. In April, the Trump administration also terminated all members of the board that steers the NSF, called the National Science Board. Former members feared that it would make way for O’Neill to stack the board with political allies, pointing to how Trump filled the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology with tech billionaires—including leaders of Meta, Google, Oracle, and Nvidia—instead of top scientists and researchers.
